solves.reasoning: (A) 'mathematics is all about abstraction' — the passage says school curriculum doesn't stress this enough, so abstraction is correct. (B) 'aim to cluster them together and study them all at the same time' — cluster (묶다) is correct, not separate. (C) 'cognitive growth' — the passage talks about mathematical thinking, so cognitive (인지적) is correct, not physical. → abstraction-cluster-cognitive = choice 1.

(A) 'instead of studying each object individually' — studying each separately (individually), not collectively. (B) 'this guarantees that every object within a class has a particular property' — guarantees (보장하다), not undermines (약화시키다). (C) 'they prove instead that it belongs to a class' — belongs (속하다), not differs. → individually-guarantees-belongs = choice 3.

(A) 'doesn't stress enough' — curriculum doesn't stress (강조하다) this. If we replace with ignore, 'doesn't ignore enough' is nonsensical. Stress is correct. (B) 'even the objects that haven't been defined yet' — defined (정의된) is correct in mathematical context. Observed is weaker. (C) 'serves as a key indicator of academic development' — indicator (지표) is correct; obstacle (장애물) contradicts the positive role described. → stress-defined-indicator = choice 3.

② 'lack' is wrong. 'belongs to a class already known to lack this property' — if the class lacks the property, there's no point proving the object has it. The passage says 'a class already known to have this property'. Lack is the opposite of what's needed.

② 'isolate' is wrong. 'aim to isolate them together and study them all at the same time' — 'isolate together' is self-contradictory. The passage says 'cluster them together'. Isolate means to separate, which is the opposite of grouping together.

③ 'differs' is wrong. 'prove instead that it differs to a class' — 'differs to' is ungrammatical (one differs from, not to), and the meaning is wrong: the proof strategy is to show the object belongs (not differs) to a known class. Passage says 'belongs to a class'.

Blank: 'aim to _____ them together and study them all at the same time.' The action groups objects together → 'cluster' (choice 4). Divide/eliminate/define don't fit 'together and study them all at the same time'.

Blank: 'this _____ that every object within a class has a particular property.' The sentence expresses a strong assurance — 'guarantees' (choice 2). Suggests is too weak; prevents/questions contradict the meaning.

Blank: 'when mathematicians want to prove that an important object _____ in a particular way.' Context: proving how an object acts/functions → 'behaves' (choice 1). Appears is too vague; fails/vanishes contradict positive proof context.

'cluster' means to group or gather things together. Context: 'aim to cluster them together' = group them together. 'group' (choice 2) is the closest synonym. Scatter means to spread apart (antonym); simplify/calculate are unrelated.

'guarantees' means to make certain or assure. Context: 'this guarantees that every object within a class has a particular property' = makes it certain. 'ensures' (choice 4) is the closest synonym. Predicts/suggests are weaker; limits contradicts.

'stress' in 'doesn't stress enough' means to emphasize or highlight the importance of something. 'emphasize' (choice 1) is the closest synonym. Relieve (opposite meaning); measure/ignore are unrelated to emphasizing.

'specific' means particular or precise (as opposed to broad). Its antonym should mean broad/non-specific. 'general' (choice 4) is the direct antonym. Particular/precise/detailed are all synonyms of specific.

'individually' means one at a time, separately. Its antonym should mean all together. 'collectively' (choice 2) = as a group = direct antonym. Separately/independently are synonyms; personally is unrelated.

(A) 'for the whole class of objects' — 'class' here = a category or group of things sharing properties = 부류 (category). (B) 'taught a class of thirty students' — 'class' here = a group of students being taught together = 학급 (classroom group). → (A) 부류 - (B) 학급 = choice 3.

Definition: 'the process of considering something at a general or theoretical level, removing specific details or concrete instances.' This describes abstraction (추상화) — the mathematical process of generalizing from specific cases. Calculation/curriculum/proficiency don't match.
Blank: 'mathematics is all about _____ (abstract)'. After 'about' (preposition), a noun is needed. 'abstract' (adjective/verb) → noun form = 'abstraction' (추상화).
Blank: 'instead of studying each object _____ (individual)'. After 'object', an adverb modifying the verb 'studying' is needed. 'individual' (adjective) → adverb form = 'individually'.

Blank: 'since all fruits have seeds, and an apple is a fruit, then _____.' This is a syllogism: if all fruits have seeds and apple is a fruit, then apple must have seeds. → 'an apple must have seeds' (choice 4). The other options don't follow the logical structure.

Blank: 'they must prove _____ only once, for the whole class of objects.' Mathematicians prove the characteristics of a class, specifically its properties. → 'properties' (choice 1). Definitions/experiments/calculations don't fit what is proved once for a whole class.
